previousCoordinate.reasonReplaced: Legacy-punktet lå nær øyas sentrum, men manglet en kildeobjektkontrakt og skilte ikke mellom øya, fortet og det maritime senteret.

identity.resolvedIdentity: Hele Isegran-øya som samlet kulturmiljø for forsvar, orlogshavn, verft, museumshavn og dagens fartøyvern.
identity.identityProblem: Navnet kombinerer flere fysiske og historiske objekter: øya, Isegran fort, tårnet, museumshavna, Bjarne Aas' båtbyggeri og dagens fartøyvernsenter. Ett fortpunkt eller én verkstedsadresse ville utelate vesentlige deler av place-recorden.
identity.splitReason: Objektene er ulike delankere innenfor samme lille, navngitte øy og sammenhengende kulturmiljø. Separate place-records kan senere opprettes dersom fortet eller fartøyvernsenteret trenger egne gameplayløp.

evidence.finding: OSM-way 198507904 identifies the named islet Isegran with representative point 59.20261, 10.94497; Wikidata and GeoNames independently identify the same island.
evidence.reason: The whole-island geometry best represents a composite place combining fortification and maritime-centre layers.

evidence.finding: The municipality describes Isegran as a strategically situated island with military structures, maritime activity, historical buildings, historic vessels, public recreation and a nationally important cultural environment.
evidence.reason: Confirms that the canonical subject is the integrated island environment rather than one isolated structure.

evidence.finding: The municipality separates the 1287 chronicle reference from the unproven medieval-castle tradition, documents seventeenth- and eighteenth-century fortification layers, the 1984–1988 tower reconstruction and the 2025 restoration.
evidence.reason: Provides the strongest source for correcting the chronology and avoiding an unsupported medieval-fort claim.

evidence.sourceName: Isegran fort entity and tower geometry
evidence.finding: Isegran fort is a named fortification subentity at approximately 59.20270, 10.94690 on the east side of the island.
evidence.reason: Used as a fort component anchor, not as the canonical point for the whole island place.

evidence.finding: The centre documents active vessel conservation, boatbuilding, restoration, rigging, bronze casting, documentation, courses and guided tours, and gives the address Mindre-Alvs vei 2.
evidence.reason: Confirms the current maritime-craft layer and access identity without replacing the island geometry.

evidence.finding: SNL identifies the island where Glomma divides, preserved fortifications, the former naval harbour, archaeological station, museum harbour and the historical association with Alv Erlingsson and Tordenskiold.
evidence.reason: Cross-checks the island identity and major historical layers.

evidence.finding: The ferry terminal at 59.20391, 10.94572 provides a public arrival anchor on the north side of the island.
evidence.reason: Retained as an access anchor rather than the place identity.

evidence.finding: The legacy coordinate is only 42.3 metres northwest of the island representative point but has no documented object role.
evidence.reason: Replaced to establish an explicit and reproducible whole-island contract.

sourceObjectCandidates.rejectionReason: Represents the fort and tower component, not the complete fort-and-maritime-centre place.
Represents the present organisation and workshop address, not all historical and public island layers.

rawEvidence.description: Persisted island geometry, fort and public-arrival anchors, chronology controls, maritime-centre identity, rejected single-component anchors and access limits.

decision.nextAction: Applied the named Isegran island geometry, retained fort and public arrival as subanchors and continued with akeroya_fort.

notes: The coordinate moves only 42.3 metres southeast but gains an explicit named-island geometry contract.
Year 1287 marks the first known chronicle reference and associated event, not a proven surviving medieval castle or the date of the current tower.
Documented fortification layers primarily belong to the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
The current tower wall is a 1984–1988 reconstruction restored and opened as a viewpoint in 2025.
Workshop, vessel and event areas may have access restrictions distinct from the public island park and ferry arrival.
The radius is not an island, fortification, harbour, property, event or safety boundary.
